solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Revealing regrettable act in two different records (10)

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so the regrettable act goes inside the second record

blocks.note: signals that two separate words for record are wanted; supplies no letters
a gramophone record is a disc
a written record is a log
a sin is a regrettable act

annotation.surface: Someone confesses a bad deed caught on two separate recordings.
annotation.walkthrough: One word, records, has to be read twice in two different senses: the kind you play and the kind a ship's captain keeps.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: making a secret known is revealing it.

entries.clue: Home evidently not cleaned without right diligence (8)

indicators.note: an old sense of without is outside, as in 'there is a green hill far away, without a city wall', so DUSTY wraps round R

blocks.note: dust is the evidence nobody has cleaned

annotation.surface: A grubby house suggests the occupant has no diligence.
annotation.walkthrough: "Without" reads as lacking, but here it means outside: the right goes in the middle of the dusty word, not away.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: steady hard work and application, as in 'praised for her industry'.

entries.clue: Man successful when racing green cycles around (3)

indicators.note: to cycle is to go round in a loop, so the front letter travels round to the back

annotation.surface: An eco-minded cyclist does well in a race.
annotation.walkthrough: Sebastian Coe is the British runner who won Olympic 1500m gold twice. Cycles belongs to the racing picture but is the instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the double Olympic champion was indeed a man who succeeded at racing.

entries.clue: Daisy Duck getting cross, I heard (5)

indicators.note: what is heard is only a sound, so I stands for a word that sounds the same

blocks.note: in cricket a duck is a score of nothing, O
a cross is the letter X
the organ of sight, said the same as I

annotation.surface: Daisy Duck, Donald's girlfriend, loses her temper.
annotation.walkthrough: Daisy Duck reads as one cartoon name, but Daisy alone is the definition and Duck gives O.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the tall white-petalled meadow flower is one kind of daisy.

entries.clue: Lacking time, change tiny bit of cash at first in town (7)

indicators.note: to be lacking something is to be without it, so time's T is missing from the change
what comes at first is the opening, so only the first letter of in is taken

annotation.surface: Someone short of time hunts for small change in town.
annotation.walkthrough: IPSWICH is the county town of Suffolk in eastern England. In looks like a link to town, but it supplies the opening letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Plainly a place of that size: the Suffolk port is a large town, not a city.

entries.clue: Our distant relatives consume fruit drinks (5,4)

indicators.note: whatever drinks takes something inside itself, so the fruit takes in the word for consume

annotation.surface: Our relatives at a party get through the fruit punch.
annotation.walkthrough: "Fruit drinks" looks like a noun phrase, juices; drinks is really the verb, and fruit its subject.
annotation.definitionFit: Humans share a common ancestor with chimpanzees and gorillas, making them relatives at some evolutionary distance.

entries.clue: Piano note organ put out daily (4)

blocks.note: the fifth note of the sol-fa scale
a newspaper is an organ; the Financial Times comes out daily

annotation.surface: A piano note and an organ are heard every day.
annotation.walkthrough: Organ belongs to the keyboard picture; in crosswords it often means a newspaper, as a mouthpiece for views.
annotation.definitionFit: A musical direction: piano on a score tells the player to play quietly.

entries.clue: Losing face, Holst struggles with Mars? Yes, in arrangement of The Planets (5,6)

indicators.note: a word's face is its front, so HOLST loses its first letter
something that struggles thrashes about out of order, so the letters are jumbled
a musical arrangement rewrites the material, so the letters are put in a new order

annotation.surface: Holst battles with his Mars movement while arranging his suite The Planets.
annotation.walkthrough: The Planets reads as Holst's orchestral suite, whose first movement is Mars; taken literally it is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain equivalent: the sun's system is made up of the planets orbiting it.

entries.clue: Polish maybe experiencing popularity, adopted by school (6)

indicators.note: an adopted child is taken into a family, so IN is taken into the school's word

blocks.note: a school is a group of fish

annotation.surface: A Pole is welcomed by a school now that they are popular.
annotation.walkthrough: Polish looks like the nationality; lower-case it is a glossy coating on furniture or nails.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example, flagged by maybe: a polish is one kind of surface coating.

entries.clue: Current and potentially endless obstacle to Labour (8)

indicators.note: something potential could become something else, so ENDLESS may turn into a new arrangement

annotation.surface: A commentator names the Labour Party's present, never-ending obstacle.
annotation.walkthrough: Labour with its capital suggests the British party; it only means work, the capital being the first word of the definition's surface.
annotation.definitionFit: Laziness gets in the way of work: nobody labours while loafing.

entries.clue: Cockney recovering part of capital (6)

indicators.note: Cockney speakers famously drop the H at the start of words

annotation.surface: A Londoner is getting over an illness.
annotation.walkthrough: Cockneys are working-class East Londoners, whose accent loses the H of words like healing.
annotation.definitionFit: The west London borough is one part of the capital.

entries.clue: Cub shedding coat with fur fit for purpose (6)

indicators.note: an animal shedding its coat loses its outer layer, so the word loses its outer letters

annotation.surface: A young animal moulting its fur is ready for anything.
annotation.walkthrough: Shedding a coat fits a furry cub so well that it is easy to miss that the word itself is being stripped.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: anything serviceable enough to be put to work is fit for purpose.

entries.clue: Area of commerce functions aboard double-decker? (3,8)

blocks.note: the affairs conducted on a large bus

annotation.surface: A trade sector asks what goes on aboard a double-decker bus.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the whimsical second half: a double-decker is a big bus, and what happens on it is its business.
annotation.definitionFit: Large corporations collectively form a sector of commerce; the second sense is a playful literal reading.

entries.clue: Grab break after unlimited cold period (8)

indicators.note: a word's limits are its first and last letters, so unlimited strips both

annotation.surface: Someone snatches a holiday after an endless winter.
annotation.walkthrough: Grab reads as seize; it is the informal sense of catching someone's attention, as in 'how does that grab you?'
annotation.definitionFit: An informal sense: something that grabs you appeals to you and holds your attention.

entries.clue: Violent resistance suppressed by Winnie the Pooh and Snow White characters (7-5)

indicators.note: a suppressed rising is held down and hemmed in, so R is enclosed by the Pooh character

blocks.note: the bouncing tiger in Winnie the Pooh

annotation.surface: Cartoon favourites put down a violent uprising.
annotation.walkthrough: Characters is plural because it covers both Tigger and the dwarf. Violent resistance looks like one phrase but the definition stops after the first word.
annotation.definitionFit: Loose but fair: someone too quick to open fire is inclined to violence.

entries.clue: Protecting millions in online financial sector (9)

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so the M sits inside the online banking word

annotation.surface: Online banks safeguard vast sums.
annotation.walkthrough: Protecting fits the surface's talk of keeping money safe; the answer protects land by building banks along a river.
annotation.definitionFit: A specialised sense: raising a bank of earth shields land from flooding.

entries.clue: Barkeeper is attractive character in melodramatic series? (4,4)

blocks.note: a dish is a good-looking person

annotation.surface: The pub landlord is the heartthrob of a TV drama.
annotation.walkthrough: Barkeeper suggests a publican; the question mark allows it to mean something that keeps a bar, of soap.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic reading: the bathroom tray keeps a bar of soap.

entries.clue: Embargo is stopping United helping City fans’ dream (12)

indicators.note: a stopper plugs a gap, so the embargo and is plug the helping

annotation.surface: A transfer embargo keeps Manchester United from helping Manchester City supporters get what they want.
annotation.walkthrough: City fans suggests football supporters; here they are simply people who love cities.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic reading: someone who loves cities would dream of towns spreading everywhere.

entries.clue: Far from cool, short anorak seen on you abroad (7)

indicators.note: something short is cut off, so the word loses its last letter
abroad means in a foreign country, so you is given in French

blocks.note: NERD without D; an anorak is a nerd

annotation.surface: Tourists abroad look uncool in short anoraks.
annotation.walkthrough: In British slang an anorak is an obsessive enthusiast, after the coats trainspotters wear. Cool here means calm, not fashionable.
annotation.definitionFit: Cool can mean calm; someone jittery is the opposite of calm.

entries.clue: Undemanding job’s axed in firm (6)

indicators.note: whatever is axed is chopped out, here the letters IN

blocks.note: a paid post needing little work

annotation.surface: An easy post has been cut at a company.
annotation.walkthrough: Firm looks like a company; it is the adjective. The 's is short for is: the easy job has IN axed.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something fixed fast and stable is firm.

entries.clue: Implore daughter leaving meal’s starter (8)

indicators.note: someone leaving walks out, so the daughter's D goes out of the meal

blocks.note: DINNER without D; the 's is has, joining the parts

annotation.surface: A parent pleads as their daughter walks out of dinner before the first course.
annotation.walkthrough: Starter seems to be the first course of the meal; it is a novice, someone starting out.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a novice who is just starting out.

entries.clue: Is a hip-hopper keeping cover of Eminem in charts again? (6)

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it, so the rapping word holds the Eminem letters inside
a cover wraps the outside, so the outer letters of Eminem are taken

blocks.note: first and last letters of EMINEM

annotation.surface: A question about a rapper covering an Eminem song that re-enters the charts.
annotation.walkthrough: Cover and charts both belong to the pop picture: a cover version, the hit parade. Here charts is a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: Charts as a verb means maps; doing it again is the re- prefix.

entries.clue: Gold going up and down dresses heading for Tina Turner (5)

indicators.note: in a down clue, a word going up is written bottom to top
clothes surround the wearer, so the two golds surround T
a heading sits at the top, so Tina gives its first letter

annotation.surface: Gold records on every side of the singer Tina Turner.
annotation.walkthrough: Tina Turner reads as the singer; Turner alone is the definition, something that turns. Or is heraldic gold.
annotation.definitionFit: Literal: the spinning part of a helicopter or engine is a thing that turns.

entries.clue: Murmur Tudor ruler gets components for arms (6)

blocks.note: Elizabeth I: ER (Elizabeth Regina) plus I

annotation.surface: A Tudor monarch quietly acquires weapons.
annotation.walkthrough: Arms suggests weapons, which suits a monarch; here they are limbs.
annotation.definitionFit: The upper-arm bones, one in each arm, are components of the limbs.

entries.clue: Another broadcast occupied by one broadcasting (2,3,3)

indicators.note: to broadcast seed is to scatter it, so the letters are scattered
a house occupied by someone has them inside, so I goes into the scattered letters

annotation.surface: A second programme is taken over by the station.
annotation.walkthrough: The first broadcast is the scattering signal; broadcasting at the end is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: a station transmitting live is said to be this.

entries.clue: Every second of service pleases pious priest (3)

indicators.note: the second letter of every following word is taken

annotation.surface: Each moment of a church service delights a devout clergyman.
annotation.walkthrough: Every second reads as each moment in time; it means the second letter of each following word.
annotation.definitionFit: A biblical figure: the Old Testament priest at Shiloh who raised Samuel.

entries.clue: It could give you a better view of French city (4)

annotation.definition: It could give you a better view

blocks.clueFragment: It could give you a better view
blocks.note: a curved glass that magnifies or focuses

annotation.surface: Something that offers a fine outlook over a French city.
annotation.walkthrough: Of looks like part of 'view of French city'; it only joins the two definitions.
annotation.definitionFit: Glasses and cameras sharpen what you see; the French town is in the Pas-de-Calais.

entries.clue: Try extremely short article penned by conservative in Reform (2,8)

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its ends, so only the outer letters of short
something penned is shut in a pen, so A is enclosed by the conservative word

blocks.note: to have a go is to try

annotation.surface: A brief piece by a Conservative writer about the Reform party.
annotation.walkthrough: Reform with its capital suggests the political party; it is the verb, as an offender might reform.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: a criminal who gives up crime and lives honestly has reformed.
